# CHANNEL STYLE PACK: How Money Works (how-money-works)
This pack describes how the reference channel writes and paces its documentaries. Use it to match the hook formula, act structure, pacing and rhetorical tone. It is a style reference: never copy its sentences, facts or topics.

# 4. STORY LABELS OF 30 REFERENCE FILMS
## HMW-20221227 — 
hook (claim, until 24.9s): The nosy auntie asking when you will marry may be doing more for your finances than you think.
thesis: Being single is becoming an unaffordable luxury for a lot of people.
beats: setup → sponsor → explainer → explainer → turn → aftermath → outro
twist: The same study finds married women earn about 10 percent less than single women, the opposite of the men's premium.
open loops: Marriage could help you earn more, or maybe a lot less, to be explained later. | Four possible explanations for the married men's pay premium. | What about married gay couples? Answer: not enough data yet.
ending: other: Marriage framed as an increasingly unaffordable investment, then a sponsor thanks and a joke about being single.

## HMW-20221231 — Blackstone and BlackRock (Stephen Schwarzman, Larry Fink)
hook (question, until 65.9s): Trillions controlled by firms you may unknowingly fund: how do they work and are they the most evil businesses in the world?
thesis: Without the ominous music and selected headlines, these are just regular investment firms like any other.
beats: setup → sponsor → rise → rise → explainer → obstacle → turn → aftermath → outro
twist: After defending both firms, the film says Blackstone might deserve some of the criticism over buying homes above asking price.
open loops: How do these companies work, and are they really the most evil? | How they make money and who they answer to. | Why the two names are confusingly similar and how the firms relate today.
ending: lesson: Neither is an evil empire nor a force for good; save anger for outright fraud, then sponsor thanks and a joke clip.

## HMW-20230110 — 
hook (question, until 34.4s): Clips on moving from ownership to access, then: how many subscriptions do you have, and how far can the model go?
thesis: Everything has become a subscription because investors love companies with a subscription service.
beats: setup → sponsor → explainer → explainer → turn → aftermath → outro
twist: After the warnings, the film argues subscriptions have probably peaked as Netflix loses subscribers and rates rise.
open loops: Why has the number of subscription companies exploded? | How far can the subscription model go? | Four reasons investors love the model.
ending: where_now: Subscriptions may fail as rates rise and customers cancel; failing businesses are not the worst outcome, then sponsor thanks and a cancellation sketch.

## HMW-20230128 — 
hook (claim, until 40.5s): Very high-IQ people can be useless through cognitive miserliness, and there is a problem with smart people making you dumber and poorer.
thesis: There is a problem with really smart people that is making you dumber and poorer.
beats: setup → explainer → sponsor → explainer → explainer → explainer → explainer → outro
twist: 
open loops: Five big problems with smart people that cost regular people money. | The false authority problem opens four much worse problems.
ending: lesson: Making people believe you are smart is lucrative; pointer to a fraud video and sponsor thanks.

## HMW-20230202 — 
hook (claim, until 58s): The school, job, promotion, retire plan is not working any more; the standard 40-year career is coming to an end.
thesis: The establishment of the 40-year career is crumbling, with some employers and employees taking advantage and others suffering.
beats: setup → explainer → explainer → explainer → explainer → explainer → explainer → aftermath → outro

# 6. NARRATIVE DEVICES (measured on 30 films' sentence transcripts)
- Cold open: hook types claim 14, question 6, irony 4, stakes 3, flash_forward 1, other 1, reversal 1. The hook runs to a median 27 s, then a one-line thesis ("This is the story of…"). Only 1/30 films open with an old date — the channel opens IN MEDIA RES (the peak, the paradox, the stakes), and only AFTER the thesis jumps back ("The story begins in…").
- Tension loops: a tension turn (a "But…/However…/And yet…" reversal, a question, "little did", "there was one problem", "would soon", "had no idea") lands every 52 s at the median (p75 123 s). Every beat ends by opening the next question; payoffs come later.
- Contrast & scale: numbers are almost never bare — they are framed against a rival, a country, a lifetime or "every person on the planet".
